question.problem:
$$

Evaluate the following integral. Do not round the answer.

${\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}\operatorname{cosh}⁡x{sech}^{3}⁡x\,\text{d}x=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
$$

First, we find the hyperbolic identity that corresponds to the trigonometric identity 

$$
\operatorname{sec}⁡x=\frac{1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}.
$$

Using Osborn's rule, the corresponding hyperbolic identity is

$$
\operatorname{sech}⁡x=\frac{1}{\operatorname{cosh}⁡x}.
$$

Now, we rewrite the integral using the above identity, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}\operatorname{cosh}⁡x{sech}^{3}⁡x\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}\operatorname{cosh}⁡x\cdot {(\frac{1}{\operatorname{cosh}⁡x})}^{3}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}\frac{1}{{cosh}^{2}⁡x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}{sech}^{2}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{tanh}⁡x\,{|}_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡2} \\  & =\operatorname{tanh}⁡(\operatorname{ln}⁡2)-\operatorname{tanh}⁡0 \\  & =\frac{{e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}-{e}^{-\operatorname{ln}⁡2}}{{e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}+{e}^{-\operatorname{ln}⁡2}}-0 \\  & =\frac{2-{2}^{-1}}{2+{2}^{-1}} \\  & =\frac{2-\frac{1}{2}}{2+\frac{1}{2}} \\  & =\frac{\frac{3}{2}}{\frac{5}{2}} \\  & =\frac{3}{5}\end{aligned}
$$
